_comment: Secondary coverage gate for the Adapter_Layer (src/adapters/**, including CommandRunner.ts and CommandController.ts) at >=85% statements; branches are not gated for this layer per the design threshold table. This is a separate config because c8 check-coverage applies a single threshold set per invocation and cannot express the Core_Layer (>=95%/>=90%, see .c8rc.json) and this Adapter_Layer gate simultaneously from one flat config. Task 8.2 runs the unit+property suite under c8 once per config so each layer is gated against its own thresholds. The gate measures in-process runtime adapters only. Excluded from the gated scope, all evidenced behaviourally by the host harnesses rather than by this metric: src/extension.ts (composition root); src/adapters/ports/** (type-only `export interface` port declarations that emit zero runtime JS); the host-only wrappers src/adapters/Vscode*.ts (thin shells over the `vscode` API that run only inside the VS Code host process); and the host-only VS Code providers src/adapters/*Provider.ts (SpecFileDecorationProvider and SpecDashboardViewProvider implement `vscode.FileDecorationProvider`/`vscode.WebviewViewProvider`, import the `vscode` namespace and carry no in-process-testable logic because their badge/color/tooltip, HTML/CSP/nonce, stats and prompt logic all live in the gate-covered pure `core/` helpers they delegate to). All excluded adapters are exercised by the @vscode/test-electron and @vscode/test-web harnesses, not by the in-process unit+property suite. Because `all: true` instruments every non-excluded source file, the type-only ports and host-only wrappers must be excluded explicitly or they would report 0% and drag the aggregate below threshold despite carrying no in-process-testable runtime logic.
